title: EM ASIA FX-Most Asian units gain ahead of Fed decision By Reuters
text:
© Reuters. EM ASIA FX-Most Asian units gain ahead of Fed decision * Optimism over U.S.-China trade talks helps support gains
* Rising oil prices hit oil-import dependent currencies - rupee, rupiah
* Thai baht at strongest level against the dollar since April 2018 (Adds text, updates prices)
By Nikhil Nainan
Jan 30 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies gained on Wednesday, on expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will signal a slower approach to rate hikes, and on hopes that Sino-U.S. trade talks this week will help de-escalate a trade war that has hurt Asian exporters.
The Fed's two-day policy meeting is due to end later in the global day, and it is widely expected to hold rates unchanged after recent comments from officials signalled a slower pace of rate increases this year. dollar index against a basket of six major currencies .DXY dipped 0.1 percent to 95.753.
Optimism over the trade talks was fanned by comments from Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook, who is in regular contact with U.S. President Donald Trump and described the trade tensions as easing this month.
Less optimistically, some investors still feared the two governments would struggle to bridge their differences after the U.S. decision on Tuesday to charge Chinese telecommunications giant Huawei Technologies Co Ltd HWT.UL with trade sanctions violations related to Iran.
China's yuan CNY=CFXS led the gains, rising 0.3 percent to 6.715 a dollar, its strongest level in over six months. Market participants regarded the yuan's stronger performance as a good omen for the trade talks, as the U.S. side does not want to see a weak yuan giving Chinese exporters a competitive advantage. MKTS/GLOB
The Philippine peso PHP= , Malaysian rinngit MYR= and Singapore dollar all strengthened 0.1 percent against the greenback.
Both the rupiah IDR= and India's rupee INR=IN , two nations dependent on oil imports, weakened 0.2 percent, hurt by a rise crude prices due to concerns over possible supply disruptions arising from Venezuela's political crisis. O/R
EMERGING ASIA'S BEST PERFORMER IN 2019 - THE THAI BAHT
The baht THB=TH strengthened 0.1 percent against the dollar to 31.473, its highest since the end of April last year.
The unit, which was the only currency among its regional peers to gain, albeit marginally, in 2018, has picked up 3.4 percent so far this year, and will likely strengthen for a third straight month.
DBS, in a note, said a combination of Bank of Thailand's policy lift-off in December, still sizeable current account surplus and impending elections have helped the baht.
The country's finance minister on Wednesday, however, cautioned that the baht should not strengthen more than currencies of other exporters. VS U.S. DOLLAR Change on the day at 0451 GMT
